questionMetadata.stem: What does prospective power describe under the specified alternative in the constructed pancreatic-cancer recurrence trial?

answerChoices.label: Chance of rejection if that alternative is true
answerChoices.rationale: Under the specified true alternative and design assumptions, power is the probability of rejecting the null. It describes how the planned procedure behaves in that situation.

answerChoices.label: Chance that a statistically positive result is true
answerChoices.rationale: This reverses what is conditioned on. Power assumes an alternative to evaluate rejection, rather than estimating whether a statistically positive conclusion is true.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This reverses what is conditioned on. Power assumes an alternative to evaluate rejection, rather than estimating whether a statistically positive conclusion is true.

answerChoices.label: Chance that the null hypothesis itself is true
answerChoices.rationale: The plan does not assign a probability to the null hypothesis being true. It calculates a rejection probability under the specified alternative.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The plan does not assign a probability to the null hypothesis being true. It calculates a rejection probability under the specified alternative.

answerChoices.label: Chance of nonrejection if that alternative is true
answerChoices.rationale: Nonrejection under a true alternative describes a type II error probability. Power instead concerns rejection under that alternative.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Nonrejection under a true alternative describes a type II error probability. Power instead concerns rejection under that alternative.

questionMetadata.explanation: Planned power is the chance of rejecting the null under the specified true alternative and design assumptions. It is not the truth probability of a positive result.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Power is the probability that the analysis rejects the null if the specified alternative is true, under the planned design assumptions. It is a statement about a procedure operating in that situation. Remember the direction of conditioning: it does not give the probability that a positive study conclusion or the alternative itself is true.

questionMetadata.patientPresentation: {patientName}, the skin-oncology journal-club lead, reviews a new topical agent for basal cell carcinoma. questionMetadata.stem: Which statement is justified when the constructed basal-cell-carcinoma recurrence trial fails to reject its null and reports low post-hoc power?

answerChoices.label: Post-hoc power does not prove no effect
answerChoices.rationale: A low post-hoc calculation does not establish that the effect is exactly absent. Power is conditional on a specified alternative, rather than a truth probability for the null.

answerChoices.label: Low post-hoc power favors an absent effect
answerChoices.rationale: The later calculation does not make the no-effect conclusion valid. Neither low post-hoc power nor nonrejection supplies proof of an absent effect.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The later calculation does not make the no-effect conclusion valid. Neither low post-hoc power nor nonrejection supplies proof of an absent effect.

answerChoices.label: Post-hoc power gives the probability of the null
answerChoices.rationale: Power does not assign a probability to the null hypothesis. It concerns rejection behavior under a specified alternative.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Power does not assign a probability to the null hypothesis. It concerns rejection behavior under a specified alternative.

answerChoices.label: The observed p-value is the study's achieved power
answerChoices.rationale: A p-value concerns observed-or-more-extreme data under a null model; power concerns rejection under an alternative. They are different conditional quantities.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A p-value concerns observed-or-more-extreme data under a null model; power concerns rejection under an alternative. They are different conditional quantities.

questionMetadata.explanation: Low post-hoc power does not prove no effect. It neither gives the probability of the null nor makes the observed p-value equal to power.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Power describes rejection probability under a specified alternative, not the probability that a hypothesis is true. A low post-hoc power calculation after nonrejection does not establish an exactly absent effect. Remember that a second conditional calculation cannot transform the first result into proof of equality or supply the effect size missing from this exercise.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: The results apply to the local test. Spreading immediately to other clinics goes beyond that scope instead of testing the next setting.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: The supplied favorable aim and balancing findings support local action. Repeating the identical pilot without acting does not use the stated learning.

The pilot aims to reduce missed lung cancers at protocol follow-up and may require extra diagnostic visits. Colleagues propose different combinations of measures for the report. The team is planning what to record before testing the unnamed program; no benefit or screening-test performance is supplied.
questionMetadata.stem: Which set lists a process measure, the intended clinical outcome measure and a balancing measure, in that order, for the lung-cancer screening program pilot?

answerChoices.label: Completed program screening; missed cancers at follow-up; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Completed screening tracks delivery, missed cancers track the program’s diagnostic aim, and extra diagnostic visits check the additional assessment burden.

answerChoices.label: Screening invitations sent; screening visits completed; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Invitations and completed screening visits both track program activity. This set does not measure missed cancers, the stated clinical aim.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Invitations and completed screening visits both track program activity. This set does not measure missed cancers, the stated clinical aim.

answerChoices.label: Completed program screening; extra diagnostic visits; missed cancers at follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Extra diagnostic visits check burden, while missed cancers measure the aim. This ordering swaps the outcome and balancing positions.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Extra diagnostic visits check burden, while missed cancers measure the aim. This ordering swaps the outcome and balancing positions.

answerChoices.label: Missed cancers at follow-up; completed program screening; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Missed cancers are the outcome and completed screening is process. This set places those two measures in the reverse order requested.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Missed cancers are the outcome and completed screening is process. This set places those two measures in the reverse order requested.

questionMetadata.explanation: Use completed program screening as process, missed cancers at follow-up as outcome, and extra diagnostic visits as balance. Attendance counts do not substitute for the diagnostic aim.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Screening activity and screening success need different measures. Completed screens track delivery; missed cancers at follow-up track the stated diagnostic aim; extra diagnostic visits check burden. Remember to count both what the program does and what it misses. Invitation or attendance totals alone do not establish that the clinical aim improved.

answerChoices.label: Arrange qualified Spanish interpretation
answerChoices.rationale: Qualified Spanish interpretation supports an understandable discussion and the patient's own questions. Neither the child's offer nor the employee's bilingual skill establishes competence to interpret clinical information.

answerChoices.label: Use the child's interpretation for consent
answerChoices.rationale: The child wants to help, but willingness does not establish the competence needed for this clinical consent discussion. The patient still needs qualified interpretation.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The child wants to help, but willingness does not establish the competence needed for this clinical consent discussion. The patient still needs qualified interpretation.

answerChoices.label: Ask a bilingual clinic clerk to interpret
answerChoices.rationale: Speaking Spanish is not itself evidence of competence to interpret clinical information. The employee's qualification has not been established.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Speaking Spanish is not itself evidence of competence to interpret clinical information. The employee's qualification has not been established.

answerChoices.label: Use a translated Spanish consent handout
answerChoices.rationale: Written information can support the discussion, but cannot provide the qualified two-way exchange needed for the patient's own clinical questions.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Written information can support the discussion, but cannot provide the qualified two-way exchange needed for the patient's own clinical questions.

questionMetadata.explanation: Arrange qualified Spanish interpretation so the patient can discuss the proposed cholecystectomy and ask questions. Neither the child's willingness nor the employee's bilingual conversation establishes interpreter competence.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Consent needs an understandable conversation, including the patient's own questions. When patient and clinician cannot communicate adequately, arrange qualified interpretation. A child's offer or an employee's conversational bilingual skill does not establish that competence. Make the conversation possible before asking for a decision; written materials can support, but cannot replace, that exchange.

A signed form lists the operation, but material risks, benefits and alternatives have not been discussed. The surgeon calls the form self-explanatory, then asks the nurse to explain its instructions. The patient has questions before agreeing to surgery.
questionMetadata.stem: With qualified interpretation in place, what is needed for informed consent to {patientName}'s laparoscopic cholecystectomy when material information has not been discussed?

answerChoices.label: Discuss risks, benefits, and alternatives
answerChoices.rationale: The patient lacks the clinical information needed to choose. Discuss the intervention's relevant risks, benefits, and alternatives, including foregoing it, in an understandable conversation.

answerChoices.label: Confirm the form was signed voluntarily
answerChoices.rationale: Voluntary signing matters, but confirming it does not supply the omitted risks, benefits, and alternatives. Information and voluntariness are separate needs.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Voluntary signing matters, but confirming it does not supply the omitted risks, benefits, and alternatives. Information and voluntariness are separate needs.

answerChoices.label: Have the patient reread the consent document
answerChoices.rationale: Rereading the document does not by itself supply the clinical conversation that never occurred. A form can document consent without replacing the discussion.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Rereading the document does not by itself supply the clinical conversation that never occurred. A form can document consent without replacing the discussion.

answerChoices.label: Ask the patient to describe the planned operation
answerChoices.rationale: Describing the procedure's purpose checks only part of understanding. The stated gaps about relevant risks, benefits, and alternatives remain.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Describing the procedure's purpose checks only part of understanding. The stated gaps about relevant risks, benefits, and alternatives remain.

questionMetadata.explanation: The missing step is an understandable discussion of the intervention, risks, benefits, and alternatives. Confirming a signature or willingness alone does not fill those information gaps.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Informed consent helps a person understand the intervention, its relevant risks and benefits, and alternatives including declining, so the person can choose voluntarily. A signature cannot replace that conversation. The patient needs that discussion before the form can be relied on for the operation. Remember: document the conversation, rather than substituting a document for it.

The patient can describe the proposed operation but has not heard the alternatives, including foregoing it. The clinic advertises a choice of appointments; both booking buttons lead to the same unavailable slot. The patient asks what other options exist.
questionMetadata.stem: With qualified interpretation in place, what information is missing before {patientName} can make an informed choice about surgery for Graves disease?

answerChoices.label: Discuss alternatives, including no procedure
answerChoices.rationale: The patient asks whether declining is an option. Discuss relevant alternatives and the implications of foregoing the operation, tailored to the situation.

answerChoices.label: Review the operation's expected diagnostic benefit
answerChoices.rationale: Expected diagnostic benefit is relevant, but repeating it leaves the question about declining and other options unanswered.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Expected diagnostic benefit is relevant, but repeating it leaves the question about declining and other options unanswered.

answerChoices.label: Review the operation's principal procedural risks
answerChoices.rationale: Procedural risks are relevant, but reviewing them alone still omits the alternatives and implications of no procedure that the patient is asking about.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Procedural risks are relevant, but reviewing them alone still omits the alternatives and implications of no procedure that the patient is asking about.

answerChoices.label: Ask the patient to choose a surgical appointment
answerChoices.rationale: Choosing an appointment assumes the procedure decision is made. The patient still needs information about alternatives before making that choice.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Choosing an appointment assumes the procedure decision is made. The patient still needs information about alternatives before making that choice.

questionMetadata.explanation: Discuss relevant alternatives, including no procedure and its implications. Repeating operation benefits or risks does not answer the patient's specific question about declining.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: A decision is informed only if the patient can consider relevant alternatives, including foregoing the proposed intervention and what that would mean. Reviewing the procedure's benefits or risks alone leaves that question unanswered. Remember to explain the choice, not only the offered procedure, using an understandable conversation tailored to the patient's situation.

questionMetadata.reachedCurrentUpdate: With qualified Spanish interpretation, {patientName}, a {patientAge}-year-old {patientSex}, is discussing biopsy of a lesion suspicious for cutaneous SCC. After hearing the explanation, the patient says the procedure guarantees no scar. The presenter promises questions are welcome, then announces that questions ended on the previous slide. The biopsy has not started, and there is time to revisit the discussion.
questionMetadata.stem: With qualified interpretation in place, what should the team do when {patientName} mistakenly expects the skin biopsy to guarantee no scar?

answerChoices.label: Clarify scarring and ask for teach-back
answerChoices.rationale: The patient has demonstrated a specific misunderstanding about scarring. Clarify it, then ask the patient to explain the plan in their own words before relying on consent.

answerChoices.label: Repeat the explanation of the biopsy technique
answerChoices.rationale: Repeating the biopsy technique does not necessarily address the supposed guarantee about scarring or check that the misunderstanding has been corrected.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Repeating the biopsy technique does not necessarily address the supposed guarantee about scarring or check that the misunderstanding has been corrected.

answerChoices.label: Ask the patient to confirm willingness to proceed
answerChoices.rationale: Willingness to proceed is different from understanding the expected result. Confirming willingness leaves the demonstrated scarring misconception unresolved.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Willingness to proceed is different from understanding the expected result. Confirming willingness leaves the demonstrated scarring misconception unresolved.

answerChoices.label: Review the signed consent form with the patient
answerChoices.rationale: Reviewing the form alone does not establish that the specific mistaken expectation has changed. Clarification and a check of understanding are needed.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Reviewing the form alone does not establish that the specific mistaken expectation has changed. Clarification and a check of understanding are needed.

questionMetadata.explanation: Clarify the mistaken scarring guarantee and ask for teach-back before relying on consent. Willingness or another reading of the form does not by itself establish corrected understanding.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: A nod or signature does not settle a demonstrated misunderstanding. Clarify the mistaken expectation, then ask the patient to explain the plan in their own words to check understanding. Here the concern is a supposed guarantee about scarring. Remember: check what the patient understood, rather than assuming that hearing an explanation means understanding it.

Information has been provided, but a companion threatens to withhold transportation unless the patient signs. In private, the patient says the study is unwanted. Testing has not started, and there is time to discuss the patient's own choice.
questionMetadata.stem: With qualified interpretation in place, how should the team respond when {patientName} privately declines nonurgent manometry after a companion threatens to withhold transportation unless the patient signs?

answerChoices.label: Pause and support the patient's voluntary choice
answerChoices.rationale: The patient privately says the procedure is unwanted after a threat about transport. Pause the elective process and support a voluntary choice rather than rely on the pressured signature.

answerChoices.label: Ask the patient to confirm consent with the companion
answerChoices.rationale: Asking for confirmation in the companion's presence preserves the setting of pressure. It does not protect the voluntary choice expressed in private.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Asking for confirmation in the companion's presence preserves the setting of pressure. It does not protect the voluntary choice expressed in private.

answerChoices.label: Offer another appointment with the same companion
answerChoices.rationale: A later appointment with the same companion does not itself address the pressure undermining consent. Changing the date is not a voluntariness assessment.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A later appointment with the same companion does not itself address the pressure undermining consent. Changing the date is not a voluntariness assessment.

answerChoices.label: Ask the companion to explain the patient's preferences
answerChoices.rationale: The companion's account cannot replace the patient's private expressed preference. Practical support does not give the companion authority to impose the elective choice.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The companion's account cannot replace the patient's private expressed preference. Practical support does not give the companion authority to impose the elective choice.

questionMetadata.explanation: Pause and support the patient's voluntary choice. The private refusal and companion's threat undermine reliance on a pressured signature for an nonurgent study with no urgent need.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Consent requires a voluntary choice as well as information and understanding. A signature obtained under the pressure described here cannot substitute for the patient's expressed preference. Pause the nonurgent process and support a voluntary decision in private. Remember that a companion's wishes do not become the patient's wishes merely because the companion provides practical support.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Possible survival is one consideration, not a complete substitute for weighing benefits, burdens, and suffering. The standard is broader than maximizing duration alone.

Remember to look for the patient's perspective first; when it is unavailable, keep the patient's welfare at the center of deliberation.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: The supplied discussion has already failed to resolve the conflict. Repeating it unchanged is not a substitute for seeking the appropriate institutional ethics support.

questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Honest disclosure separates verified facts from theories. questionMetadata.explanation: Arrange assessment, appropriate safety reporting, and protection of follow-up while supporting the clinician. Concealment or waiting for a diagnosis leaves the documented practice concern unaddressed.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Credible concerns about unsafe practice need patient protection, appropriate assessment, and reporting suited to the setting, alongside support for the colleague. Waiting for a final diagnosis does not resolve the care concern. Remember that protecting reputation cannot replace a safety response; use observed evidence without inventing the cause or treating reporting as a diagnosis.

questionMetadata.stem: What should determine the clinician's fitness to conduct {patientName}'s fissure-treatment consultation when a disability is accommodated and actual performance is safe?

answerChoices.label: Actual ability to perform the care safely
answerChoices.rationale: The relevant issue is actual safe performance, including appropriate accommodations. The scenario establishes that ability and supplies no performance concern.

answerChoices.label: The clinician's diagnosis and expected disease course
answerChoices.rationale: A diagnosis and its expected course are not by themselves a finding of inability to perform this care safely. The actual relevant duties and performance matter.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A diagnosis and its expected course are not by themselves a finding of inability to perform this care safely. The actual relevant duties and performance matter.

answerChoices.label: The clinician's ability without workplace accommodations
answerChoices.rationale: Excluding accommodations changes the supplied assessment. Safe performance with appropriate accommodations is relevant to whether the clinician can perform the duties.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Excluding accommodations changes the supplied assessment. Safe performance with appropriate accommodations is relevant to whether the clinician can perform the duties.

answerChoices.label: The patient's comfort with the clinician's appearance
answerChoices.rationale: Appearance or patient discomfort about it does not establish unsafe practice. The scenario supplies safe performance and no observed concern to support that inference.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Appearance or patient discomfort about it does not establish unsafe practice. The scenario supplies safe performance and no observed concern to support that inference.

questionMetadata.explanation: Use actual ability to perform the relevant care safely, including appropriate accommodations. The supplied safe performance does not support treating visible disability itself as impairment.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Disability and inability to practice safely are different questions. Judge the clinician's actual performance of the relevant duties, including appropriate accommodations. Here safe performance is established and no performance concern exists. questionMetadata.stem: How should the team respond when the clinician assigned to {patientName}'s dialysis-access assessment reports inability to concentrate safely and requests relief?

answerChoices.label: Arrange safe coverage and appropriate assistance
answerChoices.rationale: Arrange the available safe coverage and appropriate assistance. The clinician has recognized a current inability to concentrate safely and asked for relief before the procedure.

answerChoices.label: Reassign demanding tasks and have the clinician continue
answerChoices.rationale: Reassigning only demanding tasks still requires practice despite the stated inability to concentrate safely. It does not provide the requested relief and available coverage.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Reassigning only demanding tasks still requires practice despite the stated inability to concentrate safely. It does not provide the requested relief and available coverage.

answerChoices.label: Offer a short rest before considering relief from duty

answerChoices.distractorRationale: A rest trial postpones relief despite the clinician's stated inability and available coverage. Support the request rather than requiring further unsafe practice to demonstrate it.

answerChoices.label: Cancel the visit and defer assistance to occupational health

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Qualified coverage is available, so cancellation does not use that option. Deferring assistance also misses the colleague's current request for help.

questionMetadata.explanation: Arrange safe coverage and appropriate assistance now. The clinician has identified inability to concentrate safely, and qualified replacement care is available before the clinical consultation begins.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: A clinician who recognizes inability to practice safely should be supported in obtaining coverage and appropriate assistance. Patient protection and help for the clinician belong in the same response.

questionMetadata.stem: What should the team explain when {patientName} is told that ordinary gastric-GIST care depends on joining an optional new-biologic study?

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment does not forfeit ordinary care
answerChoices.rationale: This study is optional and not required for ordinary care. Clarify that declining enrollment does not forfeit that care, so the invitation can be considered voluntarily.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment requires transfer to another clinic
answerChoices.rationale: Requiring transfer would impose a loss of ordinary care for declining this optional study. The scenario gives no basis for making that care contingent on enrollment.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Requiring transfer would impose a loss of ordinary care for declining this optional study. The scenario gives no basis for making that care contingent on enrollment.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment postpones the surgical consultation
answerChoices.rationale: Postponing the ordinary consultation because enrollment is declined still makes care conditional on joining. That conflicts with voluntary choice in this setting.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Postponing the ordinary consultation because enrollment is declined still makes care conditional on joining. That conflicts with voluntary choice in this setting.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment limits access to routine follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Limiting routine follow-up uses ordinary care to pressure enrollment. The optional study is not required for that care.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Limiting routine follow-up uses ordinary care to pressure enrollment. The optional study is not required for that care.

questionMetadata.explanation: Clarify that declining this optional study does not forfeit ordinary clinic care. The recruiter's stated condition is inconsistent with voluntary participation in a study not required for that care.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Research participation must be voluntary. When a study is optional and not required for ordinary care, declining it should not forfeit that care. Remember to separate the clinical care decision from the research invitation. Making enrollment a condition of routine care pressures the patient instead of supporting an independent choice about participation.

answerChoices.label: Complete an appropriate research consent process
answerChoices.rationale: The additional procedure is research-only and was not discussed in the treatment consent. Address its purpose, added procedure, and voluntary choice through appropriate research consent and oversight.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Clinical consent does not expand automatically to an additional undisclosed research procedure. Extending its label does not supply the missing research discussion or applicable oversight.

answerChoices.label: Use a signed research form as the entire consent process
answerChoices.rationale: A signed research form alone is not the entire consent process. The participant needs the relevant understandable discussion and voluntary choice for the added activity.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A signed research form alone is not the entire consent process. The participant needs the relevant understandable discussion and voluntary choice for the added activity.

answerChoices.label: Ask the treating surgeon to authorize the extra sampling
answerChoices.rationale: The surgeon's approval is not the patient's research permission. It does not replace the appropriate consent process and applicable oversight.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The surgeon's approval is not the patient's research permission. It does not replace the appropriate consent process and applicable oversight.

questionMetadata.explanation: Complete the appropriate research consent process and applicable oversight before the additional sampling. The clinical-treatment signature does not automatically cover this undisclosed research-only procedure.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Consent to treatment does not automatically authorize an additional research-only procedure. The research purpose, added procedure, and voluntary choice need appropriate research consent and applicable oversight. A signature has a scope: adding a research activity requires addressing that activity, rather than extending the clinical form by assumption or treating another form as the conversation.

questionMetadata.stem: What should research consent explain when {patientName} expects personally selected treatment in a desmoid-agent trial whose protocol uses random allocation?

answerChoices.label: Assignment is random and benefit is uncertain
answerChoices.rationale: The approved protocol assigns randomly and guarantees no better arm. Clarifying both points corrects the expectation of personally selected treatment with assured benefit.

answerChoices.label: Assignment is clinical and benefit is individualized
answerChoices.rationale: The protocol does not use individualized clinical selection. This wording preserves the patient's mistaken expectation instead of explaining random allocation and uncertain benefit.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The protocol does not use individualized clinical selection. This wording preserves the patient's mistaken expectation instead of explaining random allocation and uncertain benefit.

answerChoices.label: Assignment is random and benefit is established
answerChoices.rationale: Random assignment is correct, but established benefit is not. No arm is guaranteed better in the supplied protocol.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Random assignment is correct, but established benefit is not. No arm is guaranteed better in the supplied protocol.

answerChoices.label: Assignment is chosen and benefit is uncertain
answerChoices.rationale: Uncertainty about benefit is correct, but assignment is not chosen by the surgeon or participant. The protocol uses random allocation.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Uncertainty about benefit is correct, but assignment is not chosen by the surgeon or participant. The protocol uses random allocation.

questionMetadata.explanation: Explain that assignment is random and benefit uncertain. The protocol does not let the surgeon select a personally best arm or guarantee that an arm will be better.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Research consent needs a clear account of allocation and uncertainty. This protocol assigns arms randomly; the surgeon does not choose a personally best arm, and benefit is not guaranteed. Remember to distinguish a research protocol from individually selected treatment. Understanding assignment helps the patient choose whether to join, not a detail for after enrollment.

questionMetadata.stem: How should the team respond to {patientName}'s request to leave an optional hidradenitis-agent study when unrelated ordinary appointments are threatened?

answerChoices.label: Support withdrawal and preserve ordinary follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Support the voluntary withdrawal and discuss ordinary follow-up separately. Unrelated care must not be used as leverage to require continued research participation.

answerChoices.label: Defer withdrawal until the remaining study visits are complete
answerChoices.rationale: Requiring completion of remaining visits before withdrawal makes continued participation compulsory. That does not respect the voluntary withdrawal request.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Requiring completion of remaining visits before withdrawal makes continued participation compulsory. That does not respect the voluntary withdrawal request.

answerChoices.label: Require the investigator's approval before withdrawal
answerChoices.rationale: Investigator permission is not a condition that justifies compelling continued participation. The patient wants to leave a voluntary study.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Investigator permission is not a condition that justifies compelling continued participation. The patient wants to leave a voluntary study.

answerChoices.label: Arrange transfer of ordinary care before allowing withdrawal
answerChoices.rationale: Requiring transfer first still ties ordinary care to continued enrollment. Preserve the unrelated follow-up rather than using its loss to prevent withdrawal.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Requiring transfer first still ties ordinary care to continued enrollment. Preserve the unrelated follow-up rather than using its loss to prevent withdrawal.

questionMetadata.explanation: Support withdrawal and preserve ordinary clinical follow-up. The threatened cancellation of unrelated care must not be used to compel continued participation in a voluntary study.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Voluntary participation includes being able to withdraw without coercive loss of ordinary care. Discuss ongoing clinical follow-up separately from whether research continues. Remember that stopping research participation and stopping clinical care are different choices. Neither completing unwanted study visits nor obtaining investigator permission should be used as the price of preserving unrelated follow-up.

answerChoices.label: Peer review determines the project's research classification

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Peer review evaluates a submission; it does not by itself classify the underlying activity under applicable research definitions.

questionMetadata.explanation: Explain that publication plans alone do not define research. Appropriate institutional assessment must consider the project's purpose, design, and applicable definitions rather than its intended journal destination.

questionMetadata.stem: Which examination protocol should be ordered next for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Hepatobiliary scintigraphy assessing gallbladder filling
answerChoices.rationale: Persistent local inflammatory findings call for assessment of gallbladder filling/cystic-duct obstruction despite the ultrasound components.

answerChoices.label: Hepatobiliary scintigraphy measuring stimulated ejection fraction
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Confuses evaluation of chronic gallbladder emptying with evaluation of the acute inflammatory presentation.

answerChoices.label: MR cholangiopancreatography assessing the extrahepatic ducts
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Prioritizes a duct-stone question over the gallbladder question suggested by persistent local signs; it is not a claim that MRI is never appropriate after ultrasound.

questionMetadata.explanation: The clinical findings maintain concern for acute gallbladder inflammation. questionMetadata.stem: Which evaluation plan should guide {patientName}'s next visit?

answerChoices.label: Breast assessment and medication review
answerChoices.rationale: Recognizes a focal concerning component alongside a plausible systemic explanation for the expressed bilateral secretion; an elevated prolactin does not explain away the focal episodes.

answerChoices.label: Medication review and symptom reassessment
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Over-unifies the observed patterns under a real prolactin-raising medicine and postpones assessment of the focal component.

answerChoices.label: Endocrine assessment and medication review
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Overweights the laboratory abnormality and treats it as a sufficient explanation for all of the breast observations.

questionMetadata.stem: Which combined medication plan should be agreed with {patientName}'s surgical team?

answerChoices.label: Continue ART; plan titrated intravenous midazolam with respiratory monitoring

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Preserves continuity but treats monitoring as sufficient to make the contraindicated oral combination acceptable.

answerChoices.label: Neck ultrasound surveying central and lateral nodal compartments

questionMetadata.stem: Which management plan should be initiated for {patientName}'s stoma problem?

answerChoices.label: Hospital surgical assessment with intravenous resuscitation
answerChoices.rationale: Integrates the obstructive symptoms and nonreduction; visible red bowel does not establish an uncomplicated prolapse.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Applies a conservative uncomplicated-prolapse strategy to a presentation with obstructive symptoms.

answerChoices.label: Sedated manual reduction with supervised outpatient reassessment
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Focuses on achieving reduction without first addressing the concerning obstruction/acute surgical assessment requirement.

questionMetadata.stem: Which regional-node plan should accompany {patientName}'s further excision planning?

answerChoices.rationale: Interprets the primary depth and clinically uninvolved basin, rather than treating reassuring node imaging as exclusion of microscopic involvement.

answerChoices.label: Ultrasound-guided biopsy of an imaged regional node
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Confuses size-selected sampling of a nonsuspicious visible node with mapping the sentinel drainage of the primary lesion.

answerChoices.label: Ultrasound surveillance of the regional nodes
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Overweights benign-appearing imaged nodes and omits the indicated pathologic sentinel staging discussion.

questionMetadata.explanation: The histology establishes an invasive melanoma with the supplied depth. questionMetadata.stem: Which diagnostic sampling plan should be used for {patientName}'s skin lesion?

questionMetadata.stem: Which next diagnostic action should classify {patientName}'s infiltrate?

answerChoices.label: Endoscopic resampling for histology and immunophenotyping
answerChoices.rationale: Obtains the architecture and integrated material needed to distinguish reactive and neoplastic B-cell processes and assign a subtype.

answerChoices.label: Clonality analysis using immunoglobulin gene-rearrangement testing
answerChoices.distractorRationale: May add information but cannot by itself replace morphologic/clinical correlation; clonal expansions can occur with inflammation.

answerChoices.label: Expanded immunohistochemical staining of the existing fragments
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Adds markers without repairing the absence of interpretable tissue relationships needed for integrated classification.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Moves systemic lymphoma therapy into routine initial localized infection-associated disease and substitutes a different response assessment.

answerChoices.label: H. pylori eradication with symptom-triggered clinical reassessment
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Uses the same adequate eradication treatment but mistakes symptom improvement for an adequate lymphoma-response strategy.

questionMetadata.stem: Which initial hemostatic plan should be used for {patientName}'s ulcer?

questionMetadata.stem: Which motility diagnosis best accounts for {patientName}'s returned study?

answerChoices.rationale: Integrates failed propagation with the abnormal junction-relaxation measurement rather than relying on either finding alone.

answerChoices.rationale: After an adequate endoscopic structural assessment excludes obstruction and concerning pseudoachalasia, high-resolution manometry supplies the esophageal physiology needed to evaluate suspected achalasia.

answerChoices.label: Repeat upper-GI endoscopy
answerChoices.distractorRationale: An adequate recent EGD has already excluded a mechanical explanation and concerning pseudoachalasia.

answerChoices.label: Ambulatory esophageal reflux monitoring
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Reflux monitoring does not define the suspected motility disorder.

answerChoices.label: Contrast-enhanced chest CT
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Cross-sectional imaging does not provide the required esophageal physiology after the completed structural evaluation.

questionMetadata.explanation: The selected study records pressure changes during swallowing. Interpret the returned measurements alongside the endoscopic findings.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: The selected study records pressure changes during swallowing. Interpret the returned measurements alongside the endoscopic findings.

questionMetadata.stem: Which imaging study should be arranged next for {patientName}'s intermittent groin swelling?

answerChoices.label: Ultrasound of the groin
answerChoices.rationale: Can examine the symptomatic region during positional change and straining when the lump is absent at the office examination.

answerChoices.label: Magnetic resonance imaging of the groin
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Is a plausible study for an occult cause, but is not the usual initial imaging examination in this presentation.

answerChoices.label: Computed tomography of the groin
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Provides a broader cross-sectional survey rather than the usual initial targeted assessment of an intermittent groin lump.

questionMetadata.explanation: Targeted groin ultrasound can assess an intermittent suspected hernia when examination does not establish the diagnosis. MRI can be useful after an unresolved assessment; the item does not claim ultrasound is infallible.

questionMetadata.stem: Which management plan should be recommended for {patientName}'s confirmed symptomatic groin hernia?

answerChoices.label: Elective hernia repair consultation
answerChoices.rationale: A reducible inguinal hernia causing meaningful activity limitation supports elective repair discussion and planning. The stable presentation does not require emergency treatment or a specific technique selection.

answerChoices.label: Observation with activity modification
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This patient has meaningful activity limitation rather than minimal symptoms.

answerChoices.label: Emergency exploration of the groin
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The patient is stable and the returned study identifies a reducible hernia without emergency features.

answerChoices.label: Physical therapy for presumed groin strain
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The confirmed hernia is limiting usual work or exercise and merits an elective discussion.

questionMetadata.stem: Which imaging study should be obtained before surgery for {patientName}'s papillary thyroid carcinoma?

answerChoices.label: Neck ultrasonography
answerChoices.rationale: Assesses cervical nodal compartments and local thyroid findings before operative planning.

answerChoices.label: Contrast-enhanced neck CT
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Can add information for selected extensive disease, but does not replace the initial ultrasound assessment in this stated presentation.

answerChoices.label: Thyroid scintigraphy
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Assesses thyroid tracer uptake rather than the cervical nodal anatomy needed for operative planning.

questionMetadata.explanation: Preoperative neck ultrasound is recommended for cervical nodal and local assessment after malignant thyroid cytology. Cross-sectional imaging is an adjunct when the clinical findings warrant it.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Preoperative neck ultrasound is recommended for cervical nodal and local assessment after malignant thyroid cytology. Cross-sectional imaging is an adjunct when the clinical findings warrant it.

questionMetadata.stem: Which disposition should be arranged for {patientName}'s stoma problem?

answerChoices.label: Emergency surgical assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Treats the obstructive symptoms and nonreducible prolapse as requiring acute assessment even though the bowel is still red.

answerChoices.label: Expedited outpatient colorectal assessment
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Acknowledges a surgical problem but underestimates the current obstructive presentation.

answerChoices.label: Routine outpatient ostomy assessment
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Fits appliance or uncomplicated follow-up concerns rather than this combination of vomiting, reduced output and nonreduction.

questionMetadata.explanation: Obstructive symptoms with a nonreducible prolapse warrant urgent surgical assessment. A red appearance does not remove the concern.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Obstructive symptoms with a nonreducible prolapse warrant urgent surgical assessment. A red appearance does not remove the concern.

questionMetadata.stem: Which regional-node plan should accompany {patientName}'s melanoma excision?

answerChoices.label: Sentinel lymph-node biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: Obtains regional pathologic staging for the supplied invasive melanoma thickness and nonpalpable nodes.

answerChoices.label: Lymph-node ultrasound surveillance
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Can evaluate or follow nodes in selected settings, but does not provide the same pathologic sentinel-node staging here.

answerChoices.label: Complete lymph-node dissection
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Extends nodal surgery beyond the initial staging step for clinically uninvolved nodes.

questionMetadata.explanation: The supplied melanoma thickness and nodal examination support discussion of sentinel-node biopsy with excision planning. This does not imply automatic completion dissection or a guaranteed survival benefit.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: The supplied melanoma thickness and nodal examination support discussion of sentinel-node biopsy with excision planning. This does not imply automatic completion dissection or a guaranteed survival benefit.

questionMetadata.stem: Which biopsy approach should be arranged for {patientName}'s changing pigmented lesion?

answerChoices.label: Complete excisional biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: A small accessible lesion concerning for melanoma is usually removed completely with narrow clinical margins and enough depth for histologic microstaging. Selected large or difficult lesions can require a different biopsy approach.

answerChoices.label: Superficial shave biopsy
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A superficial sample can truncate the lesion and compromise microstaging.

answerChoices.label: Partial punch biopsy
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The small accessible lesion can be completely sampled rather than selecting one potentially unrepresentative edge.

answerChoices.label: Definitive wide local excision
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Diagnostic microstaging should guide definitive planning rather than beginning with an unselected wide excision.

questionMetadata.explanation: The tissue specimen permits measurement of tumour depth and review of the excision. Use the returned histology when planning subsequent care.

questionMetadata.stem: Which operative plan should be recommended for {patientName}'s colon cancer?

answerChoices.label: Segmental colectomy with lymphadenectomy
answerChoices.rationale: Removes the tumor-bearing segment with its lymphatic drainage; normal node size on CT does not establish pathologic node negativity.

answerChoices.label: Local full-thickness excision of the tumour
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Underweights the need for regional oncologic resection and nodal assessment of an invasive tumor not suitable for endoscopic removal.

answerChoices.label: Total abdominal colectomy with lymphadenectomy
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Extends bowel removal beyond the supplied single tumor without an additional indication for total colectomy.

questionMetadata.explanation: Resection of the involved colon and its regional lymphatic drainage is the operative framework for this resectable invasive primary. CT node size does not replace pathologic assessment; additional disease or inherited risk can alter extent.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Resection of the involved colon and its regional lymphatic drainage is the operative framework for this resectable invasive primary. CT node size does not replace pathologic assessment; additional disease or inherited risk can alter extent.

questionMetadata.stem: Which staging study should be obtained before treatment planning for {patientName}'s colon cancer?

answerChoices.label: Contrast CT: chest, abdomen, pelvis
answerChoices.rationale: Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis provides standard preoperative cross-sectional staging for confirmed colon cancer.

answerChoices.label: Whole-body PET-CT for systemic staging
answerChoices.distractorRationale: PET-CT is not routine initial staging for newly diagnosed colon cancer.

answerChoices.label: Abdominal ultrasound
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Ultrasound does not provide the complete thoracic, abdominal, and pelvic staging assessment needed.

answerChoices.label: Pelvic MRI alone
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Pelvic MRI alone omits chest and abdominal staging and is not the standard complete study for colon cancer.

questionMetadata.stem: Which tissue-diagnosis plan should be arranged for {patientName}'s limb mass?

answerChoices.label: Image-guided core biopsy through a sarcoma service
answerChoices.rationale: Combines adequate tissue sampling with specialist planning of the biopsy route before a potentially malignant mass is disrupted.

answerChoices.label: Needle aspiration through a general radiology service
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Offers sampling but does not provide the planned core-tissue approach expected for the supplied suspicious deep mass.

answerChoices.label: Excisional biopsy through an outpatient surgery service
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Risks an unplanned removal before the mass and future operative approach have been coordinated.

questionMetadata.explanation: A suspicious deep mass should reach an experienced sarcoma service before biopsy. A planned image-guided core biopsy supports tissue diagnosis and an appropriate tract; MRI alone is not histologic proof.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: A suspicious deep mass should reach an experienced sarcoma service before biopsy. A planned image-guided core biopsy supports tissue diagnosis and an appropriate tract; MRI alone is not histologic proof.

questionMetadata.stem: Which imaging study should characterize {patientName}'s limb mass before tissue sampling?

answerChoices.label: Dedicated MRI of the involved extremity
answerChoices.rationale: A deep, enlarging, or ultrasound-indeterminate extremity mass warrants dedicated MRI for local characterization before biopsy. MRI guides planning but does not prove a histologic diagnosis.

answerChoices.label: Focused ultrasound of the mass
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Ultrasound has already been indeterminate or the lesion is deep and enlarging.

answerChoices.label: Plain radiographs of the involved extremity
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Radiographs can show bone or mineralization but do not provide the needed soft-tissue characterization.

answerChoices.label: Noncontrast CT of the involved extremity
answerChoices.distractorRationale: CT is not the preferred local soft-tissue characterization study in this scenario.

answerChoices.rationale: Treats the nonbleeding protruding vessel as a lesion requiring endoscopic hemostasis rather than reassurance from the dry field.

answerChoices.label: Acid suppression and planned endoscopic reassessment
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Defers hemostasis despite the supplied high-risk ulcer stigma.

answerChoices.label: Angiographic embolization and acid suppression
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Escalates to an alternative intervention before an indicated initial endoscopic hemostasis attempt.

questionMetadata.explanation: A nonbleeding visible vessel warrants endoscopic hemostasis with appropriate acid suppression. A dry field does not make it a clean-base ulcer. Angiographic embolization generally follows failed endoscopic control or rebleeding management rather than replacing the initial indicated endoscopic approach.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: A nonbleeding visible vessel warrants endoscopic hemostasis with appropriate acid suppression. A dry field does not make it a clean-base ulcer. Angiographic embolization generally follows failed endoscopic control or rebleeding management rather than replacing the initial indicated endoscopic approach.

questionMetadata.stem: Which endoscopic option should be avoided as sole treatment for {patientName}'s nonbleeding ulcer vessel?

answerChoices.label: Epinephrine plus bipolar coagulation
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This pairs epinephrine with a definitive contact-thermal modality and is an acceptable combination pathway.

answerChoices.label: Epinephrine injection alone
answerChoices.rationale: For a nonbleeding visible vessel, accepted thermal or mechanical therapy may be used alone or with epinephrine. Epinephrine alone is not definitive hemostasis, while two definitive modalities are not automatically required.

answerChoices.label: Bipolar coagulation alone
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Contact thermal therapy is an accepted monotherapy for a nonbleeding visible vessel.

answerChoices.label: Endoscopic clip alone
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Mechanical clip therapy is an accepted monotherapy for a nonbleeding visible vessel.

questionMetadata.explanation: For a nonbleeding visible vessel, accepted thermal or mechanical therapy may be used alone or with epinephrine. Epinephrine alone is not definitive hemostasis, while two definitive modalities are not automatically required.

questionMetadata.stem: Which phosphate movement best accounts for the fall in serum phosphate during this nutrition restart?

answerChoices.label: From extracellular fluid into cells
answerChoices.rationale: Connects carbohydrate-driven insulin activity with cellular phosphate uptake.

answerChoices.label: From cells into extracellular fluid
answerChoices.rationale: Reverses the compartment shift and would tend to raise the measured extracellular concentration.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Reverses the compartment shift and would tend to raise the measured extracellular concentration.

answerChoices.label: From circulating blood into urine
answerChoices.rationale: Mistakes an intracellular redistribution for renal loss after focusing on the falling serum result.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Mistakes an intracellular redistribution for renal loss after focusing on the falling serum result.

answerChoices.label: From intestinal lumen into blood
answerChoices.rationale: Confuses the source of newly absorbed nutrients with the redistribution explaining the serum fall.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Confuses the source of newly absorbed nutrients with the redistribution explaining the serum fall.

questionMetadata.explanation: After prolonged undernutrition, carbohydrate-associated insulin activity can increase cellular phosphate uptake. The relevant movement is from extracellular fluid into cells; the serum result measures the extracellular compartment.

questionMetadata.stem: Which healing strategy describes this skin-excision wound's documented course?

answerChoices.label: Healing by secondary intention
answerChoices.rationale: Recognizes healing of the open defect rather than relying on a list excluding sutures, grafting and later closure.

answerChoices.label: Healing by primary intention
answerChoices.rationale: Mistakes ordinary postoperative wound care for immediate edge approximation.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Mistakes ordinary postoperative wound care for immediate edge approximation.

answerChoices.label: Healing by delayed primary closure
answerChoices.rationale: Confuses continuing open-wound healing with an initial open interval followed by edge closure.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Confuses continuing open-wound healing with an initial open interval followed by edge closure.

questionMetadata.explanation: This course describes secondary-intention healing: the defect heals while the edges remain apart. Primary intention approximates the edges, while delayed primary closure includes later edge closure. This names the supplied course rather than recommending open healing for every excision.

questionMetadata.stem: Which initial operation is most appropriate for {patientName}'s papillary thyroid carcinoma?

answerChoices.label: Lobectomy
answerChoices.rationale: Applies the 2025 ATA initial-surgery recommendation to the stated unilateral 2 cm, intrathyroidal, node-negative and nonmetastatic profile.

answerChoices.label: Total thyroidectomy
answerChoices.rationale: Extends treatment beyond the recommended initial extent for this stated profile without another supplied indication for contralateral surgery.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Extends treatment beyond the recommended initial extent for this stated profile without another supplied indication for contralateral surgery.

answerChoices.label: Subtotal thyroidectomy
answerChoices.rationale: Treats subtotal resection as an intermediate cancer operation; it is not the recommended initial operation for this profile.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Treats subtotal resection as an intermediate cancer operation; it is not the recommended initial operation for this profile.

questionMetadata.explanation: For the stated unilateral cancer measuring 2 cm without gross extension or nodal or distant metastases, the 2025 ATA recommendation supports lobectomy as the initial operation when surgery is chosen. Bilateral cancer or other indications can change the operation. This choice follows disease extent rather than an answer-directing tissue-preservation request.

questionMetadata.stem: Which test should be completed before {patientName}'s adrenal biopsy?

answerChoices.label: Plasma free metanephrines
answerChoices.rationale: Evaluates the catecholamine-related hazard before the planned invasive sampling.

answerChoices.label: Overnight dexamethasone suppression
answerChoices.rationale: Selects cortisol assessment from the adrenal hormonal workup rather than evaluating catecholamine secretion.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Selects cortisol assessment from the adrenal hormonal workup rather than evaluating catecholamine secretion.

answerChoices.label: Plasma aldosterone-renin ratio
answerChoices.rationale: Selects a mineralocorticoid workup from a different adrenal decision pathway.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Selects a mineralocorticoid workup from a different adrenal decision pathway.

questionMetadata.explanation: Pheochromocytoma must be assessed before a biopsy of an indeterminate adrenal mass when tissue would change management. Plasma free metanephrines address that risk; urinary fractionated metanephrines are another accepted approach, but are not offered here. Cortisol or aldosterone evaluation answers different questions.

questionMetadata.stem: Which statistical test is most appropriate for comparing recurrence between the study groups?

answerChoices.label: Fisher exact test
answerChoices.rationale: Interprets the small observed categorical table and the inadequacy of the usual large-sample approximation.

answerChoices.label: Pearson chi-square test
answerChoices.rationale: Recognizes independent categorical groups but overlooks the sparse expected-count problem.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Recognizes independent categorical groups but overlooks the sparse expected-count problem.

answerChoices.label: McNemar test
answerChoices.rationale: Recognizes a binary outcome but mistakes the two independent groups for paired observations.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Recognizes a binary outcome but mistakes the two independent groups for paired observations.

questionMetadata.explanation: Fisher exact testing fits this small two-by-two table from independent groups. Expected counts derived from the observed margins are too sparse for the usual Pearson approximation in this exercise. McNemar testing would require paired binary observations. The invented counts do not establish clinical efficacy.

questionMetadata.stem: Which measure is calculated by the expression in this ulcer-recurrence report?

answerChoices.label: Odds ratio
answerChoices.rationale: Recognizes the ratio of two odds, rather than a direct comparison of probabilities.

answerChoices.label: Risk ratio
answerChoices.rationale: Treats division of odds as though it were division of the probabilities themselves.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Treats division of odds as though it were division of the probabilities themselves.

answerChoices.label: Risk difference
answerChoices.rationale: Confuses a relative comparison with subtraction of the two probabilities.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Confuses a relative comparison with subtraction of the two probabilities.

questionMetadata.explanation: Each p/(1-p) term is an odds. Dividing the two terms produces an odds ratio. A risk ratio divides the probabilities themselves, and a risk difference subtracts them. Similarity in selected settings does not make these measures interchangeable.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Each p/(1-p) term is an odds. Dividing the two terms produces an odds ratio. A risk ratio divides the probabilities themselves, and a risk difference subtracts them. Similarity in selected settings does not make these measures interchangeable.

exhibit.title: Fictional comparison expression
exhibit.body: Let p_E denote recurrence probability in the exposed group and p_C recurrence probability in the comparator group. The reported expression is [p_E / (1 - p_E)] / [p_C / (1 - p_C)].

questionMetadata.stem: Which mechanism best explains the recorded end-tidal CO2 change?

answerChoices.label: Absorption from the insufflated cavity
answerChoices.rationale: Connects insufflation with a new systemic CO2 load requiring ventilatory clearance.

answerChoices.label: Rebreathing from the anesthetic circuit
answerChoices.rationale: Interprets elevated expired CO2 as inspired-gas contamination despite the supplied inspiratory tracing.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Interprets elevated expired CO2 as inspired-gas contamination despite the supplied inspiratory tracing.

answerChoices.label: Production from increased metabolic activity
answerChoices.rationale: Attributes the change to endogenous production rather than the insufflated gas and temporal pattern.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Attributes the change to endogenous production rather than the insufflated gas and temporal pattern.

questionMetadata.explanation: CO2 from the insufflated cavity can be absorbed and add to the systemic load requiring ventilation. The temporal pattern and recorded observations favor that mechanism here. An unexpected or acute perioperative deterioration still requires assessment rather than automatic attribution to insufflation.

questionMetadata.stem: During a routine colonoscopy, you find a smooth subepithelial lesion with normal overlying mucosa and a faint yellow hue. It feels soft, indents with gentle pressure from closed biopsy forceps, and then regains its shape. What is the most likely diagnosis?

answerChoices.distractorRationale: A neuroendocrine tumor is not identified by the approved combination of a soft yellowish lesion and positive cushion sign.

answerChoices.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor

questionMetadata.explanation: A soft, yellowish subepithelial lesion that indents and rebounds demonstrates a characteristic cushion or pillow-sign phenotype that strongly supports colonic lipoma.

questionMetadata.stem: Which colonoscopy description most strongly supports a colonic lipoma?

answerChoices.distractorRationale: This vascular-appearing profile is not the approved characteristic lipoma phenotype.

questionMetadata.stem: The lesion has a characteristic endoscopic appearance of a colonic lipoma. The patient has no pain, bleeding, ulceration, obstructive symptoms, or other concerning features. What is the most appropriate lipoma-directed plan?

answerChoices.label: Segmental colectomy
answerChoices.distractorRationale: An operation is not indicated solely for the approved clear asymptomatic phenotype.

questionMetadata.explanation: A clearly characterized asymptomatic lipoma does not require lesion-directed treatment or dedicated surveillance. Other findings and ordinary screening indications still determine routine follow-up.

questionMetadata.stem: Colonoscopy demonstrates a clearly characterized colonic lipoma with normal overlying mucosa. The finding is incidental, and the patient has no symptoms attributable to it. What should you recommend for this lesion?

answerChoices.label: A patient with a lesion causing obstructive symptoms

answerChoices.distractorRationale: The complete imaging assessment, not one descriptor, determines the final category.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Large rod-like calcifications are categorized as typically benign.

answerChoices.label: Coarse, densely calcified, confluent calcifications
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This coarse densely calcified profile is categorized as typically benign.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Vascular calcifications are categorized as typically benign.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Rim calcifications are categorized as typically benign.

answerChoices.label: Layering calcifications
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Layering calcifications are categorized as typically benign.

questionMetadata.explanation: Fine pleomorphic morphology is suspicious; the other listed patterns are categorized as typically benign.

questionMetadata.patientPresentation: A patient is seen after mammography has identified breast calcifications. The imaging descriptors are already available, and the question is which profile is typically benign.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Fine pleomorphic calcifications are a suspicious morphology.

answerChoices.label: Fine linear-branching calcifications
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Fine linear or fine linear-branching calcifications are a suspicious morphology.

answerChoices.label: Coarse heterogeneous calcifications
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Coarse heterogeneous calcifications are in the suspicious lexicon rather than the typically benign group.

questionMetadata.explanation: The coarse densely calcified pattern is typically benign. The other listed morphologies are in the suspicious lexicon.

questionMetadata.patientPresentation: A patient presents with diagnostic mammography results describing calcification morphology and distribution. No biopsy result is available.
questionMetadata.stem: Which statement about a segmental distribution of breast calcifications is most accurate?

answerChoices.label: It is a distribution descriptor that must be interpreted with calcification morphology and the complete imaging assessment; it does not by itself diagnose cancer
Segmental distribution automatically confirms breast cancer
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Distribution alone does not provide tissue diagnosis.

answerChoices.label: Calcification distribution has no role in imaging assessment
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Distribution is an imaging descriptor that contributes to the complete assessment.

answerChoices.label: Every diffuse calcification pattern requires tissue diagnosis
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The complete morphology and imaging assessment determine whether tissue diagnosis is indicated.

questionMetadata.explanation: Distribution modifies interpretation but does not replace morphology, the rest of the examination, or tissue diagnosis when indicated.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: MRI is not the appropriate sole initial imaging plan for this scoped presentation.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: A new persistent palpable mass in this age group warrants diagnostic imaging.

questionMetadata.patientPresentation: A nonpregnant, nonlactating 38-year-old woman at average breast-cancer risk presents with a newly noticed discrete breast mass without erythema, drainage, or other overt inflammatory findings.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: PET/CT is not the appropriate initial breast imaging approach for this scoped presentation.

answerChoices.label: Proceed directly to surgical excision before diagnostic imaging
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The approved pathway begins with diagnostic imaging rather than cancer-directed surgery without imaging or tissue diagnosis.
